whatItIs.text: A small, sour green citrus — really several species, most sold as seedless Persian limes; the juice and zest cut through rich food like nothing else.

historyNote.text: Limes originated in tropical Southeast Asia and rode the Austronesian expansion across the Pacific (c. 3000-1500 BC); British sailors later ate them against scurvy so faithfully that 'limey' became their nickname, a closely guarded military secret.

howToChoose.text: Choose limes that feel heavy and give slightly; smaller Key limes are more aromatic, Persian limes juicier and seedless.

storage.text: Refrigerate in the crisper, or juice and freeze in cubes. The rulebook has the details.
storage.note: storage windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Roll a dry lime before juicing to get the last out; spent halves scrub cutting boards and limescale, and the zest flavours almost anything before the fruit goes in the compost.

substitutions.note: sweeter, sunnier acidity; slightly less sharp
